news.title:
India's cement sector saw steady FY26 performance, driven by infrastructure demand, efficiency, and capacity expansions.
Key players like UltraTech Cement, Grasim, and Ambuja Cements posted revenue and profit growth, supported by sustainability and operational focus.

UltraTech Cement, Shree Cement posted stable Q4FY26 aided by demand, price recovery, and leverage benefits.
West Asia conflict-induced input cost pressures began surfacing toward Q4FY26 end.
SHREECEM: Higher P/E Expectations And Dividends Will Shape Balanced Future Returns
news.body: Analysts have lifted their price target for Shree Cement from ₹21,386 to ₹22,392, citing updated assumptions on revenue growth, profit margins and future P/E that together support a higher fair value estimate, despite a slightly lower discount rate. What's in the News A board meeting is scheduled for May 6, 2026 to consider audited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and year ending March 31, 2026, and to consider recommending a final dividend for FY 2025-26 on the equity shares of the company.

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: EPS misses analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹483 (up from ₹311 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹216.0b (up 12% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹17.4b (up 55% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 8.1% (up from 5.8% in FY 2025). The increase in margin was driven by higher revenue. Revenue was in line with analyst estimates. Earnings per share (EPS) missed analyst estimates by 4.0%. Revenue is forecast to grow 4.8% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 1.9% decline forecast for the Basic Materials industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 3% per year whereas the company’s share price has increased by 1% per year.

news.title: SHREECEM: Upcoming Board Actions And Subsidiary Plan Will Support Undervalued Upside
news.body: Analysts have trimmed their price target on Shree Cement from ₹28,479.03 to ₹27,727.85 after applying a slightly higher discount rate and assuming a lower profit margin, partly offset by updated expectations for revenue growth and future P/E. What's in the News Board meeting scheduled on May 6, 2026 to review audited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and year ending March 31, 2026, and to consider recommending a final dividend for FY 2025-26 on the equity shares, if any (company filing).

news.title: SHREECEM: Higher Discount Rate And Lower Future P/E Will Pressure Returns
news.body: Analysts have reduced their fair value estimate for Shree Cement from ₹22,717.66 to ₹21,386.18. This change reflects updated assumptions on discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E expectations.

news.title: SHREECEM: Upcoming Board Decisions Will Support Undervalued Long Term Upside
news.body: Analysts have adjusted their view on Shree Cement, trimming the price target slightly from ₹28,602.53 to ₹28,479.03. This reflects a modestly higher discount rate, a marginally lower profit margin outlook, and a broadly unchanged revenue growth assumption alongside a similar forward P/E multiple.

news.body: Analysts have trimmed their price target on Shree Cement from about ₹30,458 to roughly ₹28,603, reflecting updated views on growth, profitability, discount rate and future P/E assumptions. What's in the News A board meeting is scheduled on Mar 16, 2026 to consider incorporating a wholly owned subsidiary in Mauritius, indicating potential changes in the company’s corporate structure or international presence (company filing).

news.title: SHREECEM: Plant Lockout Resolution And Modest Multiple Reset Will Shape Returns
news.body: Analysts have trimmed their fair value estimate for Shree Cement slightly from about ₹22,748 to roughly ₹22,718, citing updated assumptions around discount rates, revenue growth, profit margins, and future P/E levels. What's in the News Management declared a lockout at the Baloda Bazar cement plant in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, effective 18 December 2025, citing non co operation from workmen.

news.title: SHREECEM: Recent Lockout And Lower Earnings Multiple Will Pressure Future Returns
news.body: Analysts have trimmed their fair value estimate for Shree Cement from ₹24,263 to ₹22,748, citing updated assumptions around revenue growth, profit margins, and a lower future P/E multiple. What's in the News Management declared a lockout at the Baloda Bazar cement plant in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, effective 18 December 2025, after reporting non co operation from workmen.

news.title: SHREECEM: Resolved Baloda Bazar Lockout Will Support Future Earnings Rebound
news.body: Analysts have trimmed their fair value estimate for Shree Cement to ₹35,697 from ₹38,433, reflecting updated views on its revenue growth assumptions, profit margins and expected future P/E multiple. What's in the News Management and workmen at the Baloda Bazar cement plant in Raipur, Chhattisgarh reached an amicable settlement, and the company withdrew the lockout effective 22 December 2025 at 11:00 PM (company filing).
